claims.text: Removing Co from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi increases the effective stacking-fault energy of the resulting FeNiCrMn alloy.
Removing Co reduces alloying-induced lattice distortion in FeNiCrMn relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Reduced lattice distortion leads to a higher effective stacking-fault energy.
Higher effective stacking-fault energy enhances dislocation cross-slip.
Enhanced cross-slip promotes dynamic recovery during deformation.
Cross-slip and dynamic recovery become especially influential at elevated temperatures and higher strain rates.
The Co-free alloy has reduced deformation-twinning activity relative to the CoCrFeMnNi baseline.
The Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy will exhibit lower strain hardening than equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi at elevated temperatures and higher strain rates.
The predicted reduction in strain hardening is caused by increased dynamic recovery through cross-slip.
Reduced twinning contributions may reduce the ductility of FeNiCrMn relative to the baseline.
The proposed mechanism modifies the strength–ductility balance of FeNiCrMn under dynamic loading relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
The hypothesis is intended to apply between approximately 20°C and 600°C and between strain rates of 10^-4 s^-1 and 10^3 s^-1.
Outside the stated temperature and strain-rate ranges, additional deformation mechanisms may dominate.
